items.title: Michael White interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 10, 2025
items.q: I didn’t hear George Lewis live. ... So no I never got to hear him live. I got to play with a lot of people that played with him and they told me things about him. But it wasn’t really until I accidentally stumbled on and bought a record of his, and when I heard that it completely changed my life.

ctx.x: How did you learn the repertoire that was required to play the gigs that you just mentioned?

Oh, trial and error. It was like being thrown in the water. The first job I played for four years was with a brass band with Ernest “Doc” Paulin’s Brass Band. And 90% of our work was for sessions I mentioned, community social club parades, jazz funerals, and church parades. And I had been listening to records like the Atlantic recordings “Jazz © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

Begins” with the Young Tuxedo Brass Band from the late 1950s. And luckily I started practicing with that and a number of the songs that Doc played were on that recording. Other songs you know I learned by trial and error. You find out that songs have chord structures, you’re in a certain key, you have the chord structure and you kind of figure out what the chords are. And then you kind of play along with those chords. You listen to recordings, I listened to a lot of recordings to kind of figure out what the role…
